land.label: Buying land
land.title: Buying land for your unit
land.q1: Can I use this land for my planned industry?
land.q2: Will I get CLU approval for this plot?
land.q3: What should I check before paying a token or signing the registry?
land.helps: Rapid checks your plot and land records against your proposed activity, so you know the approval route before committing.
land.warning: A plot can’t be changed after registry. Get a 48-hour check first.

machinery.label: Planning machinery or expansion
machinery.title: Planning new machinery or an expansion
machinery.q1: Do my consents need to change before I add machinery or capacity?
machinery.q2: Should I check subsidy conditions before I place the machinery order?
machinery.q3: Will my project report and finance papers match the new investment?
machinery.helps: Rapid reviews your plan against your existing consents and the schemes that may apply, so you know the order of steps before you order.
machinery.warning: Some scheme conditions depend on dates. Check them before you place the order.

newUnit.label: Setting up a new unit
newUnit.title: Setting up a new unit
newUnit.q1: Which approvals does my unit need, and in what order?
newUnit.q2: Can I start construction while an application is pending?
newUnit.q3: Which schemes may be relevant to my project?
newUnit.helps: Rapid maps the approvals your activity and site need, then sets out the order and dates so each application is ready when it is due.
newUnit.warning: Approvals depend on each other. Starting out of order can hold up the project.

running.label: Unit already running
running.title: Keeping a running unit in order
running.q1: Which renewals are coming up, and by when?
running.q2: Are there subsidy or incentive claims I should be filing?
running.q3: Is the cover on my plant and machinery still right?
running.helps: Rapid keeps track of your renewal dates and claim windows, and prepares the filings so nothing lapses.
running.warning: A missed renewal or claim window can mean a penalty or a fresh application.

fileStuck.label: Approval file stuck
fileStuck.title: An approval file that has stopped moving
fileStuck.q1: Why has my application not moved?
fileStuck.q2: What does the department still need from me?
fileStuck.q3: Should I follow up, correct the file or apply again?
fileStuck.helps: Rapid reviews your file and the correspondence so far, finds what is holding it up, and tells you what to send and to whom.
fileStuck.warning: Find out what is holding it before you pay anyone to chase it.

claimStuck.label: Subsidy claim stuck
claimStuck.title: A subsidy claim that has stopped moving
claimStuck.q1: Is my claim file complete, with the documents in order?

claimStuck.q3: What follow-up is needed with the department or the bank?
claimStuck.helps: Rapid checks the claim file against the scheme conditions and prepares the follow-up needed for the next step.
claimStuck.warning: Claim windows can close. Check the dates early.

faq.title: Before we begin.
faq.intro: A few useful answers before your first conversation with Rapid.

subsidies.q: Which subsidies could apply to my business?
subsidies.a: The relevant schemes depend on your business activity, location, investment and project dates. Rapid reviews those details, identifies suitable opportunities and takes ownership of the agreed application work.

both.q: Can Rapid help with both subsidies and approvals?
both.a: Yes. Rapid works on approvals, subsidy applications and the follow-ups in between, so your documents and dates stay in one plan. The scope of each assignment is agreed with you before work begins.

when.q: When should I speak to Rapid about a new unit or expansion?
when.a: Before you commit to land, machinery or construction. Some approvals and scheme conditions depend on the order and timing of those steps, so an early conversation helps you plan them properly.

name.q: Do I need to know the scheme or approval name?
name.a: No. Tell Rapid what you plan to build, buy or expand, and where. Rapid identifies the approvals and schemes that may be relevant and explains the next step.
